annotation.walkthrough: Rachel Reeves is the Labour Chancellor of the Exchequer, fond of blaming the Conservatives' legacy. The answer runs on into 8 down.
annotation.definitionFit: Reeves, as Labour Chancellor, routinely attributes the country's financial problems to the previous Tory government.

entries.clue: Doctor, I had sex, needing only half of my erectile state (8)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person being addressed, but it is a verb meaning falsify. I'D comes straight from 'I had'.

entries.clue: see 18dn. (5)

annotation.surface: A tabloid hack desperate for a story, turning to phone-hacking or other snooping.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about press intrusion; the definition is a joke, since an endoscope literally goes into the body's private places.
annotation.definitionFit: An endoscope is a camera tube passed inside the body, so it literally invades the privates.

entries.clue: Lover-boy Macron, disconcerted, about to change direction (8)

indicatorNotes.disconcerted: thrown into confusion, the letters of Macron are jumbled

annotation.walkthrough: 'About to change direction' reads as Macron on the verge of a policy U-turn; it is RE followed by an instruction to reverse it.
annotation.definitionFit: A romancer is someone who woos, a lover-boy.

entries.clue: Ham's finished at function (7)

blocks.note: when something is finished it is over
to function is to act, operate

annotation.surface: A leftover ham finished off at a party or reception.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ham' reads as cold meat at a buffet, but it is a verb: to ham is to overplay a role. 'Function' is likewise a verb, not a social event.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ham is to play a part with exaggerated, theatrical excess.

entries.clue: "Kamala-Trump ends with lap dancing!" shock (5)

indicatorNotes.ends: take only the end letters of Kamala and Trump
indicatorNotes.dancing: the letters of lap move about, as dancers do

annotation.walkthrough: Kamala Harris and Donald Trump were rivals in the 2024 US election; the quoted headline is itself the shocking thing.

entries.clue: Mark's erect, able to screw (9)

annotation.surface: A bloke called Mark boasting he is up for sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a man's name but is the verb, as in marking an anniversary.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of observing an occasion, as in marking a birthday.

entries.clue: see 1ac.
US haircut given by doctor, an aggressive sort (6)

blocks.note: a hawk is one who favours force, as against a dove

annotation.surface: A spiky haircut handed out by a combative doctor.
annotation.walkthrough: The US name for the crest of hair is Mohawk; British English usually calls it a Mohican, hence 'US'.
annotation.definitionFit: A Mohawk is the American name for a shaved head with a central crest.

entries.clue: Pompous relative Ed is fussed about nothing (9)

annotation.definitionFit: Grandiose means pompous, pretentiously grand.

entries.clue: Incredibly supple pensioner's initially missing a beat (5)

indicatorNotes.Incredibly: done incredibly, the letters are rearranged beyond belief

indicatorNotes.missing: that letter is removed from supple

annotation.walkthrough: One of SUPPLE's two Ps goes, and the remaining SUPLE is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the throb felt at the wrist is a beat of the heart.

entries.clue: Uniform: force needs to get rid of unflattering cap (5)

entries.clue: One ball I've injured, with one wrapped on hand (9)

indicatorNotes.wrapped: one more A is taken into the mix

annotation.walkthrough: Both 'one's become A, and all nine letters are rearranged together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is on hand can be had or used right now.

entries.clue: Heap of grass gives tense American a hit (7)

blocks.note: to sock someone is to punch them

annotation.surface: A pile of cannabis leaves an edgy American a hit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' and 'hit' suggest drugs; grass is literal here and a hit is a punch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a dense clump or mound of grass.

entries.clue: Number two's prompted by its relaxation (9)

annotation.definition: Number two's prompted by its relaxation

blocks.note: reads as a deputy, but 'number two' is nursery slang for a bowel movement

annotation.walkthrough: 'Number two' reads as a second-in-command, but it is nursery slang for defecation.
annotation.definitionFit: Relaxing the anal sphincter is what lets a bowel movement happen.

entries.clue: Italian's nutsack strained after getting end away (6)

indicatorNotes.strained: strained, the letters are pulled out of shape
indicatorNotes.getting end away: the end letter, K, is removed

blocks.note: last letter of nutsack, removed to leave NUTSAC

annotation.surface: An Italian man's scrotum under strain after getting his end away, slang for having sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply drops the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone from Tuscany, the region round Florence, is one kind of Italian.

entries.clue: Maybe Georgia fell about somewhere in the palace? (9)

indicatorNotes.Maybe: Georgia is just one example of the class STATE
indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to face the other way, so MOOR is read backwards

annotation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but it is the northern English noun for a hill moor.
annotation.definitionFit: Staterooms are the grand ceremonial rooms of a palace.

entries.clue: (& 2dn.) Poll turnover article by Hunt – get on with it! (3,2,3)

blocks.note: to poll is to cut off the hair or horns
T/O is the business abbreviation for turnover

annotation.surface: A pollster's figures on voter churn and an article by a politician named Hunt, with an impatient reader urging haste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poll' and 'Hunt' dress up as an election survey and Jeremy Hunt, the Conservative politician, but they are plain verbs here. The answer runs on into 2 down.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from old films, which were told to skip the dialogue and go to the chase scene: stop dithering.

entries.clue: Starmer welcomes start of honeymoon stage with cool indifference (6)

indicatorNotes.start of: take the first letter of honeymoon

annotation.walkthrough: Starmer is Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister from 2024; the 'honeymoon stage' sounds like his early days in office.

entries.clue: Miserable Cameron on being replaced by a bastard: "Grim" (7)
